arms: fine_tuned:seed0..2 (base intfloat/multilingual-e5-small, prefix 'query: ', TrainConfig defaults, epochs 2, hard negatives: up to 5 TF-IDF top-50 neighbours of dev entities)

data.source: GLEIF LEI-CDF 3.1 Golden Copy, publish 2026-11-21 08:00 UTC, CC0 1.0

exclusions: SOLE_PROPRIETOR entities (people's names); registrations ANNULLED or DUPLICATE
follow_up_not_in_this_rule: whether the lei_global model transfers to lei_africa
known_ceiling: a previous legal name can share nothing with the current one (a rebrand); no string method can retrieve those, which lowers the ceiling for every arm equally
question: Does a fine-tuned encoder retrieve organisations by their registry-asserted other names (previous, trading, transliterated, other-language) better than character TF-IDF?
sampling: lei_global: salted-hash sample of 4,000 of 504,350 entities outside Africa; lei_africa: all 2,053 African entities; <= 8 names per entity; names folded for de-duplication

splits.rule: dev if int(sha256(lane + '\0' + entity)[:8], 16) % 2 == 0 else test
splits.unit: entity (Wikidata QID); every name of one item is in one split

why_e0d: GLEIF publishes alias labels asserted by registration authorities; E0b's Wikidata lanes showed a large gain but did not transfer to facilities, so organisations get their own lane with their own data
